body:
Unfortunately we cannot change the default values beacus it would break compatibility.

I will take a look if we can NaN the transform instead of zero'ing it.

I have a small reproduction of a potentially related CPUParticles3D visibility problem. In this case the particle has emitting=false from scene load and is never started, yet a billboard quad is visible in both the editor and when running the scene.

The attached project contains one CPUParticles3D (amount=1), a built-in QuadMesh with an unshaded billboard material (Keep Scale disabled), an explicit visibility AABB, and a camera. No script is attached to the scene and no external assets are required.

Steps: import project.godot with Compatibility, open main.tscn, and run it without enabling emission. Expected: no particles. Actual: a white square at the center.

Reproduced on official 4.7.1 (a13da4feb), 4.7.2 (ed1daf0bf), and 4.8 beta1 (4d10419ca), Windows 11 / RTX 3060 / NVIDIA 580.88 / OpenGL Compatibility. The optional verifier observes visible_instances=-1; setting it to 0 removes the artifact (900 changed pixels).

A local 4.7.1 patch initializes/uploads the CPU particle buffer and preserves zero visible instances when redraw is disabled in set_amount(). It removes this reproduction and passes 17 supplemental lifecycle checks, including resizing, emission, completion, restart and destruction with a separate render thread.

Related prior work: #66115 initializes CPU particle data on the 3.x branch; #120230 initializes the underlying MultiMesh buffers. Zero initialization alone does not prevent this billboard from being rendered while the instance count remains visible.

This may be a narrower case than the start/stop behavior originally reported here. Would this reproduction belong in this issue, or should it be tracked separately? I am not claiming that the local patch fixes every inactive-particle billboard case.

I also tested source commit 679066724352c12673001d692d41dc2dab9314c0 (master as checked on 2026-10-21), building it both unmodified and patched. Unmodified master reproduces the issue in the editor and runtime; the patch removes it. Compatibility runtime: 900 changed pixels before versus 0 after. Editor viewport: 5702 versus 0. Vulkan Mobile with the safe render thread: 900 versus 0. Patched master passes all 17 supplemental lifecycle checks with a separate OpenGL render thread. These are Windows desktop tests, not mobile-device tests.

Disclosure: the investigation, reproduction tooling, proposed patch, testing, and this comment were authored by OpenAI Codex on my behalf.

### Minimal reproduction
[stopped-cpu-particles-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33758085/stopped-cpu-particles-mrp.zip)

![White billboard visible although emission was never enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b5584f5-f92b-4a8e-a3a3-0f70fb358323)

### After the fix (same master with the patch)
![No particle visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3ceab6be-b923-4c44-bf25-725733d662bd)
I believe this is the same issue.
